subject: Logging & redaction controls — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@fintechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Logging & redaction controls — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the security/data handling items we discussed: 

Summary of requirements you flagged: 
- Redact PII from request and response logs (examples: SSNs, credit card numbers, account numbers, full email addresses in free text).
- Remove or mask identifying headers and trace IDs before logs are persisted.
- Log retention: short retention window for raw logs containing sensitive values (you suggested 30 days), with aggregated metrics retained longer.
- Support for data residency (US-hosted) and customer-managed keys for any stored raw artifacts.
- SOC2 evidence and controls description for logging/retention/redaction flow.

Proposed approach from our side (high-level):
- Offer two redaction modes: (1) SDK/client-side masking (recommended for max control), (2) server-side ingestion redaction (for legacy integrations).
- Default to masking headers and removing trace IDs at ingestion time; raw payloads (if retained) would be encrypted with CMK and only retained per the agreed SLA window.
- Provide configuration flags per environment: retention_days_raw, retention_days_aggregated, enable_header_masking, enable_traceid_strip.

Next steps / asks from you: 
1) Confirm the fields you consider PII (we listed a few above) and any additional patterns to redact.
2) Confirm the retention windows you want for raw logs vs aggregated metrics (you suggested 30 days raw).
3) Confirm whether you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or Redwood-managed encryption is acceptable for the trial.

I'll attach a short controls doc and a draft SLA for your review. If that looks good, Neha can propose a technical implementation plan and timeline next week.

Thanks — happy to jump back on a quick 30-min call if needed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

Attachments: redaction_controls_v1.pdf, SLA-draft.docx

From: Alice Chen <alice@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Security Team <security@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Logging & redaction controls — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful, appreciate the clear recap. Answers inline / additional notes below: 

PII / fields to redact (confirmed):
- Full SSNs, full credit card numbers, bank account numbers, and any government IDs.
- Full email addresses when they appear in free-text user messages, but user_id hashed/tenant_id ok to keep for analytics if pseudonymized.
- Any customer-specific tokens (auth tokens) or session cookies must be stripped from headers before persistence.

Trace IDs / headers:
- We cannot keep full trace IDs in persisted logs. We prefer either (a) strip trace IDs at ingestion or (b) replace with a non-reversible hash that cannot be used to re-identify a session.

Retention windows:
- Raw logs containing PII: 30 days (hard requirement).
- Aggregated metrics/usage counts: 13 months.

Encryption / keys:
- We strongly prefer customer-managed keys (KMS) for any raw artifacts that are stored even temporarily.

Audit / evidence: 
- Please include a short SOC2 control mapping for the redaction flow. Our procurement team will need it for security review.

SLA / commercial:
- We are still evaluating but would like a draft SLA that calls out the retention and delete procedures and an escrowing process for key rotation.

If you can send the controls doc and the draft SLA, I’ll route to our security and procurement teams. I can also schedule a short follow-up next week (Tue/Wed) with our security lead.

—Alice
Alice Chen
Head of Integrations | FintechCo
alice@fintechco.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Logging & redaction controls — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alice / Marissa — looping in some technical detail and options so procurement/security have something concrete to review. Attaching the redaction controls doc (redaction_controls_v1.pdf) and a draft SLA (SLA-draft.docx).

Technical implementation options (tradeoffs):
1) SDK / client-side masking (recommended):
   - Client (FintechCo) integrates our SDK that performs deterministic hashing or regex-based masking before sending requests.
   - Pros: PII never leaves the client, minimal changes to our server pipeline, simplest for compliance.
   - Cons: Requires engineering changes on your side.

2) Server-side ingestion redaction: 
   - Redwood inspects incoming requests and applies pattern-based redaction + header trimming before writing logs. Raw payloads optionally encrypted with customer-managed keys and stored only for the configured retention window.
   - Pros: Works with existing integrations; centralized controls.
   - Cons: Requires strong auditing and key management, slightly higher risk surface.

3) Hybrid: client-side masking + server-side verification and sampling.

Specific controls we can enable/configure: 
- enable_header_masking: true/false
- enable_traceid_strip: true/false (or replace-with-nonreversible-hash)
- retention_days_raw: integer (e.g., 30)
- retention_days_aggregated: integer (e.g., 395)
- cmk_kms_key_id: string (customer-managed key)
- redact_patterns: list of regex patterns (we can provide defaults and accept custom patterns)

Audit & evidence: 
- We can provide a SOC2 control mapping for the redaction flow plus a short implementation diagram.
- All admin actions (turning flags on/off, accessing raw artifacts) are logged in our audit trail.

Proposed mutual action plan (dates tentative):
- By Fri 6/11: FintechCo confirms final PII list, retention windows, and KMS preference.
- By Wed 6/16: Redwood provides a technical implementation plan + target config flags and timeline for a pilot.
- Week of 6/21: Start pilot (limited traffic) with agreed redaction mode.

Attachments: redaction_controls_v1.pdf (controls), SLA-draft.docx (commercial + retention language).

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with our infra team (Rishi) and your security lead to walk the flow.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai
